title: Netcatty Plugin Contract
description: Canonical public contract for Netcatty plugin manifests and host RPC messages.

JsonValueLimits.description: Host-enforced structural limits for every plugin protocol JSON value.

WireIntegerLimits.description: Host-enforced integer precision limit for JSON protocol fields used in identity, ordering, and correlation.

RpcLimits.description: Host-enforced byte limit for one JSON-RPC control message. Larger payloads must use a stream.

StreamLimits.description: Host-enforced identifier and byte limits for stream frames.

TerminalInterceptorLimits.description: Host-enforced byte and receive-window limits for the privileged direct terminal interceptor MessagePort.

ImporterLimits.description: Host-enforced byte and record limits for one importer operation.

SyncLimits.description: Host-enforced byte and identifier limits for one encrypted sync-object operation. inlineObjectBytes is the maximum ciphertext size that may travel inline on the control plane (below the 128 KiB provider JSON budget after base64 expansion).

ContributionId.description: A globally unique contribution id. Semantic validation requires the exact '<pluginId>.' prefix.

PluginHostProtocol.description: A host protocol owned by a connection Provider contribution: plugin:<providerId>.

SecretRef.description: A host-issued reference to secret material. The random identifier is opaque and never sufficient authority on its own. The non-secret key binds permission authorization to the packaged manifest resource; privileged consumers must revalidate identifier ownership, key binding, and operation scope.

CredentialRef.description: An opaque host-issued reference to a Netcatty-owned credential. The host validates ownership and provider-operation scope before issuing a plaintext lease.

SecretLeaseRef.description: An opaque, operation-bound, single-consumption lease. Only a host capability broker can consume it after revalidating runtime identity and operation scope.

SemverRange.description: A node-semver compatible range. Official consumers must also run semantic validation.

NonResourceScopedPermission.description: A permission whose complete activation-time scope is represented by the permission name itself.

ResourceScopedPermission.description: A permission whose approval must be constrained to explicit canonical resources.

PermissionResource.description: A host-canonicalized permission resource. Filesystem resources may be absolute platform paths; other permission kinds impose narrower runtime limits.

BoundedPermissionResource.description: An explicit resource bound; the all-resources wildcard is not an activation-time bound.

PermissionResourceKind.description: Whether a canonical resource grant covers only that resource or a filesystem directory subtree.

RequiredPermissionDeclaration.description: Required resource-scoped permissions must name their complete activation-time approval bounds.

ContextKeyExpression.description: A host-parsed Context Key expression. Plugins must not evaluate this string themselves.

ConnectionControlResult.description: resize, signal, reconnect, and close are acknowledged by returning JSON null. Any object result is rejected.

credentialId.description: Source id of an identity or key draft in the same import. Netcatty maps it to the newly persisted host-owned credential id.

ImporterHostDraft.description: A host draft normalized by Netcatty before Vault persistence. Executable startup commands and plaintext built-in credentials are intentionally not part of this public importer shape.

RpcRequest.description: A generic request. Reserved methods with dedicated schemas are excluded and must validate against their exact contract.

RpcNotification.description: A generic notification. Reserved notifications with dedicated schemas are excluded and must validate against their exact contract.

RpcMessage.description: A mutually exclusive RPC wire envelope. Reserved inbound methods use their exact schemas. Successful responses require method-specific validation through request correlation.
